pool.text: Determine the equation of the oblique asymptote to the graph of \( f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 3x + 4}{x - 1} \).

pool.exam_archetype: Functions (HL Extensions) — Direct Concept & Representation
pool.sol: To find the equation of the oblique asymptote, divide the numerator by the denominator using polynomial long division or synthetic division: \[ \begin{aligned} 2x^2 - 3x + 4 &= 2x(x - 1) - x + 4 \\ &= 2x(x - 1) - (x - 1) + 3 \\ &= (2x - 1)(x - 1) + 3 \end{aligned} \] Dividing through by \( x - 1 \) yields: \[ f(x) = 2x - 1 + \frac{3}{x - 1} \] As \( x \to \pm\infty \), the remainder term \( \frac{3}{x - 1} \to 0 \). Therefore, the linear quotient gives the oblique asymptote: \[ y = 2x - 1 \] - \( y = 2x - 3 \) arises from mistakenly dividing each of the first two terms by \( x \) directly without performing proper polynomial division. - \( y = 2x + 1 \) arises from a sign error when subtracting \( -2x \) during the division step. [M1] [A1]

Dividing through by \( x - 1 \) yields: \(f(x) = 2x - 1 + \frac{3}{x - 1}\) As \( x \to \pm\infty \), the remainder term \( \frac{3}{x - 1} \to 0 \). Therefore, the linear quotient gives the oblique asymptote: \(y = 2x - 1\).

pool.sol: The vertex of a parabola given by \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) is at \( \left( -\frac{b}{2a}, f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right) \right) \). We are given that the vertex is at \( (-1, 8) \). Therefore, \( -\frac{b}{2a} = -1 \), which implies \( b = 2a \). We are also given that the vertex is at \( y=8 \), so \( f(-1) = 8 \). Substituting \( x = -1 \) into the function: \( a(-1)^2 + b(-1) + c = 8 \implies a - b + c = 8 \). Since \( b = 2a \), we have \( a - 2a + c = 8 \implies -a + c = 8 \). The graph also passes through the point \( (1, 0) \). So, \( f(1) = 0 \). Substituting \( x = 1 \) into the function: \( a(1)^2 + b(1) + c = 0 \implies a + b + c = 0 \). Now we have a system of equations: 1) \( b = 2a \) 2) \( -a + c = 8 \) 3) \( a + b + c = 0 \) Substitute (1) into (3): \( a + 2a + c = 0 \implies 3a + c = 0 \). Now we have a system with \( a \) and \( c \): -a + c = 8 3a + c = 0 Subtract the first equation from the second: \( (3a + c) - (-a + c) = 0 - 8 \implies 4a = -8 \implies a = -2 \). Substitute \( a = -2 \) into \( b = 2a \): \( b = 2(-2) = -4 \). So, \( a = -2 \) and \( b = -4 \). Common algebraic traps include: - Incorrectly applying the vertex formula. - Errors in solving the system of linear equations. - Confusing the x and y coordinates of the vertex. [M1] [A1]
